guideTitle: 6 Best Large Rain Barrels for 100 Gallons and More in 2026
metaDescription: Six ways to store 100 gallons or more of rainwater, from collapsible 100 to 132 gallon tanks to a 60 gallon rigid barrel and a two-barrel 100 gallon set.
introParagraphs: Standard rain barrels hold about 50 to 60 gallons, which a single storm can fill several times over. If your roof is large or your garden is thirsty, you want 100 gallons or more, and there are two practical ways to get there: one big collapsible tank, or two rigid barrels linked together. Each has a different set of tradeoffs for weight, durability and cost.

This lineup covers six options. The VEVOR holds 100 gallons with seven support rods and an overflow kit, two YYLXTEX 100 and 132 gallon tanks use 2 mm poles and thick three-layer PVC, the VINGLI holds 100 gallons with a PVC frame and mesh fabric, the Step2 Lakewood is a 60 gallon rigid barrel with a stand that you can link to a second, and the RTS ECO two-pack gives you two 50 gallon barrels with stands and a link kit for a 100 gallon system.

We evaluated each one based on product specs and buyer feedback, concentrating on structure, material, fittings and how each reaches its capacity. A full 100 gallon tank weighs about 800 pounds and a 132 gallon tank over 1,000, so base strength and levelness are not optional. Rain barrel water is non-potable, so keep it for gardens, lawns and washing the car.

products.name: VEVOR 100 Gallon Collapsible Rain Barrel 1000D PVC

specList.label: Fittings
specList.value: Three pre-installed outlet valves, overflow kit

products.description:
The VEVOR is a 100 gallon collapsible barrel made of 1000D waterproof PVC that the listing says is UV-resistant and non-toxic, with high-temperature sealing and a rated range of minus 30 to plus 70 degrees Celsius. Seven 2 mm support rods and a lotus base are designed to keep it stable when fully loaded. A transparent body with scale lines lets you check the water level, and a wide mesh top keeps leaves out.

The kit includes three pre-installed outlet valves, an overflow kit, and sealing tape that you are told to use for better leak resistance. Two taps give fast access to water for gardens and emergency use. The tradeoff is weight, since a full tank is about 800 pounds, and a soft tank can bulge on an uneven base. Sealing tape and several valves also mean more joints that need checking each season.

For ownership, prepare a firm, level pad and drain the tank before freezing weather, then fold it for storage. Compared with the YYLXTEX 100, it lists rod count and an overflow kit rather than wall thickness. Compared with the RTS two-pack, it is one unit but not rigid. Compared with the VINGLI, it adds a transparent level gauge and more valves.
products.bestFor: Gardens that want 100 gallons in one folding tank with a level gauge and overflow kit.
pros: Seven rods, lotus base, overflow kit
cons: Several valves and tape seals to check
Soft walls need a perfectly level base

products.name: YYLXTEX 100 Gallon Collapsible Rainwater Collection Barrel
specs: 5 mm mesh screen and quick-connect tap
products.description:
The YYLXTEX 100 gallon tank is reinforced with 2 mm thickened support poles and a 0.6 mm three-layer PVC body with a high-density woven liner. A 5 mm mesh screen blocks debris at the top, and reinforced sealing covers all seams and the quick-connect spigot. The listing claims it can cut outdoor water costs by 20 to 30 percent, which is the maker's estimate, not a measured result.

The woven liner and thick PVC target tear resistance, the main durability concern with soft tanks. The kit includes a quick-connect hose, a collapsible bucket, a sprinkler, and plant labels, and the listing says setup takes under 5 minutes. The tradeoff is that overflow is not described, so you must plan your own overflow route. A full tank is about 800 pounds, and the soft design still needs a smooth, level base.

For ownership, clear sharp objects from the pad and check the screen after leaf fall. Compared with the VEVOR 100, it documents wall thickness and a woven liner but lacks a described overflow kit. Compared with the 132 gallon YYLXTEX, it is smaller and lighter. Compared with the VINGLI, it adds the quick-connect kit and a stated mesh size.
products.bestFor: Buyers who worry about punctures and want the thickest documented body.
pros: 0.6 mm three-layer PVC with woven liner
cons: Cost saving claim is the maker's estimate

products.name: YYLXTEX 132 Gallon Collapsible Rainwater Collection Barrel
products.description:
The YYLXTEX 132 gallon is the largest tank here, using the same 2 mm thickened support poles and 0.6 mm three-layer PVC body with a woven liner as the 100 gallon version. A 5 mm mesh screen filters debris, and the kit adds a quick-connect hose, sprinkler, and collapsible bucket. The listing says it can cut outdoor water costs by 20 to 30 percent, which is a maker claim.

Extra capacity means you capture more of a big storm and water longer between rains. The same structural spec as the smaller tank applies to the larger volume. The tradeoff is weight, since a full tank is over 1,000 pounds, which demands an exceptionally firm, level base. It takes a big round footprint, and overflow handling is essential at this size, yet the listing does not describe an overflow outlet.

For ownership, plan for overflow and a drain path before the first storm. Fold it flat for winter after draining. Compared with the 100 gallon YYLXTEX, it adds 32 gallons for more weight. Compared with the VEVOR 100, it holds one third more and documents wall thickness. Compared with the Step2 at 60 gallons, it holds more than double in a single unit.
products.bestFor: Large roofs and big gardens that need the maximum folding capacity.
pros: 2 mm poles and thick PVC with woven liner
Full kit with hose and sprinkler

products.description:
The VINGLI is a 100 gallon collapsible barrel with a PVC frame and anti-corrosion PVC mesh fabric designed for long-term use, including cold winters. Two rubber rings come with each spigot and water outflow valve, one installed inside and one outside the barrel, to prevent leakage. A top mesh keeps leaves and insects out of the water, and a sibling listing adds a filter spigot and overflow kit.

The double rubber ring system targets leaks at the fittings, which is where soft tanks most often fail. A PVC frame holds the shape and the foldable design stores in a garage or utility room. The tradeoff is that the listing gives no wall thickness or rod count, so structure is less documented than the YYLXTEX or VEVOR. A full tank is about 800 pounds.

For ownership, tighten fittings per the instructions and check the rubber rings seasonally. The outflow valve can connect to another VINGLI barrel to add capacity. Compared with the VEVOR 100, it emphasizes seals over rods. Compared with the YYLXTEX 100, it documents less on wall thickness but offers linking. It suits buyers worried about leaks.
products.bestFor: Buyers whose main worry is leaking fittings.
cons: Wall thickness and rods not stated
Fewer kit extras than the YYLXTEX

products.name: Step2 Lakewood 60 Gallon Rain Barrel With Stand
products.description:
The Step2 Lakewood is a rigid 60 gallon barrel on an integrated stand. A stainless steel mesh screen filters fine particulate, and a durable 3/4 inch brass spigot is included. Double-walled plastic construction resists chipping, fading, cracking, and peeling, and assembled dimensions are 46 inches high by 24 wide by 20 deep.

The elevated design improves water pressure and makes filling a watering can easier, and you can link multiple barrels together for increased storage and overflow management. Linking two Step2 barrels would give 120 gallons with rigid walls, a stand, and a brass spigot on each. The tradeoff is that a single barrel holds only 60 gallons, so reaching 100 or more requires buying and linking more than one. Each full barrel weighs over 500 pounds, and it is not collapsible.

For ownership, plan a firm, level base for each barrel and a link kit, and wipe the plastic down occasionally. Drain it before the first freeze and leave the spigot open. Compared with the collapsible tanks, it is more durable but less flexible. Compared with the RTS two-pack, it has a stainless screen and brass spigot, while the RTS lists a plastic spigot.
products.bestFor: Buyers who prefer rigid barrels and will link two for 120 gallons.
pros: Rigid double-walled 60 gallon barrel with stand

products.name: RTS Home Accents 50 Gallon ECO Rain Barrel 2-Pack
products.description:
The RTS ECO 2-pack includes two 50 gallon rain barrels with a stand and link kit for larger water storage needs. They are made from 100 percent recycled UV-resistant polyethylene with a flat back shape that fits snugly against walls and fences. A built-in overflow valve ensures safe overflow management and prevents flooding.

Two flat-back barrels give you a 100 gallon system with rigid walls and a clear linking path, and each barrel comes with a stand to raise the spigot for a watering can. The tradeoff is that the listing describes a plastic spigot and no screen, so you may want to add a mesh cover. Two barrels need two spots, and the set ships in more than one package. Each full barrel is heavy.

For ownership, place both on level bases, link the overflow, and screen the openings to keep mosquitoes out. Compared with the Step2, it offers two barrels but a plastic spigot and no stated screen. Compared with the collapsible tanks, it is rigid and not foldable. It suits buyers who want a modular 100 gallon setup.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want a modular 100 gallon system from two rigid barrels.
pros: Built-in overflow valve and link kit
cons: Ships in more than one package

buyingCriteria.explanation: You can reach 100 gallons with a single collapsible tank like the VEVOR or with two rigid 50 gallon barrels like the RTS ECO 2-pack. A single tank has fewer fittings but soft walls, while two barrels are rigid but need a link kit. The Step2 at 60 gallons can be linked for 120. Choose by durability needs and the space you can give to a base.

A full 100 gallon tank weighs about 800 pounds, and a 132 gallon tank over 1,000. A full 55 gallon barrel weighs over 400 pounds, and the 60 gallon Step2 weighs more than 500. The base must be level, firm and clear of sharp debris, because tipping or settling is the biggest risk at this scale. Compact gravel or a paver pad works better than bare soil.

Soft tanks rely on rods and thick PVC. The VEVOR uses seven 2 mm rods and a lotus base, the YYLXTEX uses 2 mm poles and 0.6 mm three-layer PVC with a woven liner, and the VINGLI uses a PVC frame. Rigid barrels like the Step2 avoid the problem entirely. Check for stated thickness, and inspect folded tanks for creases before filling.

Fittings are the weak point of any barrel. The VINGLI uses two rubber rings per spigot and outflow valve, the VEVOR ships sealing tape and three valves, and the Step2 uses a 3/4 inch brass spigot. Low spigots need elevation for watering cans, which is why the Step2 and RTS include stands. Inspect fittings each season.

A big tank fills fast in a storm and must have an overflow route. The VEVOR includes an overflow kit, the RTS ECO has a built-in valve, and the Step2 links barrels. Direct overflow away from the foundation. Most YYLXTEX and VINGLI listings do not detail overflow, so plan a diverter or a second barrel.

Collapsible tanks fold flat, which simplifies winter storage. Rigid barrels must be drained and stored or tipped. Freezing can crack spigots and walls, though the VEVOR lists a rated range down to minus 30 degrees Celsius. Drain fully before the first hard freeze and leave spigots open.

howWeEvaluated.title: Capacity
howWeEvaluated.description: We used stated volumes. The YYLXTEX 132 leads, the VEVOR, YYLXTEX 100 and VINGLI hold 100, the RTS 2-pack totals 100, and the Step2 holds 60 per barrel. We note that all full-weight figures are simple water math, not the maker's claims.

howWeEvaluated.title: Structure
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated support. The VEVOR lists seven 2 mm rods and a lotus base, the YYLXTEX models list 2 mm poles and 0.6 mm PVC with a liner, the VINGLI lists a PVC frame, and the Step2 is rigid double-walled plastic.

howWeEvaluated.title: Fittings
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked sealing and spigots. The VINGLI uses double rubber rings, the Step2 uses a brass spigot, the VEVOR ships sealing tape and three valves, and the YYLXTEX uses a quick-connect tap.

howWeEvaluated.title: Overflow
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at overflow details. The VEVOR has an overflow kit and the RTS 2-pack has a built-in valve. The YYLXTEX tanks do not describe overflow.

howWeEvaluated.title: Value
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed documented features. The YYLXTEX models were the best documented bodies, the VEVOR the best documented kit, and the Step2 the best documented hardware.

faq.q: How heavy is a 100 gallon tank when full?
faq.a: About 800 pounds, and a 132 gallon tank over 1,000. A full 55 gallon barrel is over 400 pounds. Use a level, firm, debris-free base, and never place a full tank on a raised platform that is not rated for it.

faq.q: Is one big tank or two barrels better?
faq.a: One tank has fewer fittings but soft walls, and two barrels are rigid but need a link. Both reach 100 gallons. Choose by durability and storage.
Yes. A big tank fills fast, so direct overflow away from the foundation. The VEVOR includes an overflow kit and the RTS ECO has a built-in valve, while other listings leave it to you.

faq.q: Is rain barrel water safe to drink?
faq.a: No. It is non-potable and meant for gardens, lawns and car washing. Roof debris and bird droppings mean it should never be used for drinking or cooking. Keep a fine mesh over every opening.
Drain fully, dry it and fold collapsible tanks. Leave spigots open on rigid barrels. Freezing cracks fittings, so reconnect the downspout for the cold months.
Thicker PVC with a woven liner resists punctures and seam stress. The YYLXTEX lists 0.6 mm three-layer PVC with a liner, and the VEVOR lists 1000D PVC. A thin tank can fail at the seams when full.

faq.q: How do I keep mosquitoes out?
faq.a: Cover every opening with fine mesh and keep the lid tight. The VEVOR has a wide mesh top, the YYLXTEX a 5 mm screen, and the Step2 a stainless screen. Mosquitoes need several days of standing water, so empty and refresh the barrel regularly.
